quality_guards: Work-related stress risk depends on demands, control, support, relationships, role, change, individual factors and organisational context.
HSE stress evidence is organisation-, role-, worker-, management-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Diesel-exhaust risk depends on engine type, fuel, load, temperature, ventilation, task duration, maintenance and worker exposure.
HSE diesel-exhaust evidence is engine-, workplace-, task-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer probability.
Sharps risk depends on device, procedure, contamination, handling, disposal, worker competence, protective controls and response time.
HSE sharps evidence is device-, procedure-, patient-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Workplace-violence risk depends on sector, task, public contact, lone working, environment, staffing, controls and local incident patterns.
HSE violence evidence is workplace-, task-, worker-, offender-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level assault probability.
Norovirus risk depends on setting, contact patterns, surface contamination, hygiene, outbreak status, age, immunity and timing.
UKHSA norovirus evidence is outbreak-, setting-, person-, genotype-, surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Invasive-GAS risk depends on strain, clinical syndrome, contact intensity, setting, host factors, wound status and response timing.
UKHSA iGAS evidence is case-, contact-, setting-, organism-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Hepatitis-B risk depends on vaccination, exposure route, viral load, contact type, host factors, setting and follow-up timing.
UKHSA hepatitis-B evidence is patient-, exposure-, laboratory-, vaccination-, care- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Self-feeding-product risk depends on design, flow rate, infant position, age, caregiver control, product condition and response time.
OPSS self-feeding evidence is product-, design-, infant-, use-, clinical- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level choking probability.
Volcanic-ash risk depends on concentration, particle properties, route, engine and airframe type, exposure duration, weather and operator controls.
CAA volcanic-ash evidence is eruption-, forecast-, airspace-, aircraft-, operator- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
SPAD risk depends on signal layout, train speed, braking, driver performance, adhesion, overlap, protection systems and operating context.
ORR SPAD evidence is event-, route-, signal-, train-, driver-, protection- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
